findings.text: follow-on: the script reproduces assemble_pf_currents' scaling inline (currents = currents * pf_current_scales) instead of calling operator.assemble_pf_currents, so the 'raw channel unit -> amperes' conversion now lives in two places. The two agree today (verified read-only: operator.pf_amc_channels equals the script's channel list, and scales[13.725 x4, 8.875, 9.625, 15.4375, 22.0625, 9.5, 11.25] pair correctly), but the alignment is implicit -- it holds only because _jt60sa_coil_channels() returns the channels in alphabetical order, which is also sorted(pf_by_chan)'s order. A channel list in a different order would silently mis-scale every coil. Calling assemble_pf_currents per time slice, or asserting the channel order, would remove the assumption.

follow-on: the MAST default path regenerates 2 nominal-table / 12 reconstruction / 5 null against the committed receipt's 2 / 14 / 3. The node discloses this and argues the range-representative candidate build is neutral (representation key equal per range), so both differences predate the node. Reproduced: the head run prints 2/12/5; the receipt's two flips are the single borderline loop fl_p5l_1 (margin +0.000475 [+0.000193,+0.000785] committed vs -0.000313 here, both ~1e-3). The base at f94bc702 raises LookupError on the MAST default path, so the pre-node MAST verdicts cannot be re-derived directly and the 'predate this node' claim is argued from neutrality, not measured. The receipt should be regenerated and relanded once the follow-on is settled.

follow-on (coverage): the change has no automated test. The angle-route repair (removal of the direct magnetics.nc read) and the per-column scale application are exercised only by the reviewed run's manual script invocations; a regression would be caught only by re-running the script and noticing the verdict counts move. The swap-control raise is the one in-script guard, and it does fire (verified). A test that read_geometry_table supplies every JT-60SA probe angle (non-None) would pin the route the first review found broken.

justifications.durability: The change carries one in-script guard and it is non-vacuous: forcing the superseded no-change control pair (magPbTC1/magPbTC2) makes the run raise RuntimeError and exit 1 (reproduced), so the control is shown to fail when the fit stops responding. The |r| correction is verified to move the verdict distribution from 3 identity / 0 negate / 41 undecided to 3 / 1 / 40, i.e. negate becomes reachable. But there is no automated test: the angle route and the scale application are guarded only by re-running the script, and the scale/channel alignment is implicit (see the duplication follow-on).
justifications.evidence: The gates named in the manifest ran and their results reconcile: ruff on the script EXIT=0; the JT-60SA run EXIT=0 with 3/1/40 and 2 changed verdicts under swap; the MAST --output-root run EXIT=0 with 2/12/5. I reproduced all three independently: the jt60sa run in a scratch tree returns identical verdict counts, and the regenerated jtmm-vacuum-adjudication.json and .html are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed artifacts (diff empty), so the committed evidence is genuinely the script's output at this revision. The swap-control guard was shown to fire by mutation (exit 1). Soft spots: the MAST receipt mismatch is disclosed but not measured against a pre-node MAST run (the base crashes), and the change carries no test.
justifications.fit: The docstring on _jt60sa_operator and the regenerated evidence fragment state the mechanism (selector supplies axes; operator scale carries the turn totals) and the fragment honestly quantifies the borderline MAST flip. Two fit costs: the inline re-implementation of assemble_pf_currents' conversion, and the implicit reliance on pf_amc_channels being alphabetically sorted for the scales to pair with the right coil. The new --output-root option is documented in argparse help and reuses NOTE_PATH/FIGURE_ROOT by rebasing them, which is tidy.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Plan section 6's node brief is that the repair reads probe angles through read_geometry_table, applies the root-cause correction, runs MAST's default path into a scratch directory and compares with the committed receipt, and replaces the swap control with one whose verdict can change. All four are done and reproduced: the direct netCDF4 read of magnetics.nc is gone (grep finds only a docstring mention) and read_geometry_table supplies the axes; the MMSYS currents are multiplied by operator.pf_current_scales = [13.725 x4, 8.875, 9.625, 15.4375, 22.0625, 9.5, 11.25], the deck turn totals the drive-topology repair declared; the verdict rule now tests |pearson_r| so the negate branch is reachable, and magFlxLp7 lands negate at slope -0.986/-1.086/-0.988 with r -1.000/-0.995/-0.999; and the swap control is the differing pair magFlxLp7/magPbTC8. The re-run returns 3 identity / 1 negate / 40 undecided over E100595, E100579, E100642, matching the node's claim exactly.
justifications.reuse: The node extends existing owners rather than adding a parallel source of truth: read_geometry_table's probe_angle_source branch supplies the angles (retiring the script's second supplier), build_operator's pf_current_scales supplies the turn factor, and --output-root rebases the existing NOTE_PATH/FIGURE_ROOT constants. It removes _jt60sa_probe_angles outright. The one duplication is the inline scaling noted above.
